summary: Phase 1 refactor regression test - routes/social_profile.py extraction. All 9 extracted endpoints (public-profile, privacy-settings, follow, unfollow, check-follow, followers, following, feed/global, feed/network) + 5 regression endpoints (dashboard, user, community/posts, recent-activity, auth/login) + 1 cross-endpoint follows consistency check all PASSED. 19/19 pytest cases green on first run.

minor.issue: When 'Already following' idempotent path is taken, no new social_activities record or notification is written - but also no duplicate follow_id row. Matches original server.py behaviour; not a regression.
If user follows >1000 users, the following list is silently truncated by .to_list(1000). Pre-existing behaviour, carried over as-is from server.py.

critical_code_review_comments: routes/social_profile.py (413 lines) is clean, self-contained, and follows the DRY rule - the _list_relations() helper correctly deduplicates followers/following logic which was duplicated in original server.py. Good refactor quality.

Local helper _create_social_notification in social_profile.py duplicates (partially) the global create_social_notification in server.py. Ok for phase 1 isolation but should be consolidated in phase 2 into a shared /app/backend/utils/notifications.py module to avoid drift.

set_db(database) global mutation pattern is used (same as other extracted routers). Works for FastAPI single-process but makes unit testing harder - future phases should consider passing db via FastAPI dependency injection (Depends).

Router registered without a prefix (api_router.include_router(social_profile_router) - paths in file already start with /users/... and /feed/...). Matches existing pattern; verified endpoints resolve correctly with /api prefix via api_router.
Badge/level computation is embedded inline in get_public_profile; consider extracting a pure util so it can be reused by /api/feed/* if needed (minor).
